title: Denser ≠ Better: Limits of On-Policy Self-Distillation for Continual Post-Training
hook: On-policy self-distillation was supposed to fight forgetting in continual post-training — instead, denser self-distillation can drift further off course and collapse outright.
key_points: Continual post-training tries to add new knowledge without erasing old capabilities; on-policy self-distillation (a model scoring its own generations) looked like a promising stabilizer.
Revisiting this via 'self-distillation policy optimization' (SDPO): it speeds up in-domain specialization when teacher signals are stable, but generalizes poorly out-of-distribution.
In continual post-training, SDPO forgets more than plain on-policy RL like GRPO, and can collapse outright — GRPO adapts more conservatively and preserves prior capabilities better.
Denser self-distillation causes larger drift in both parameter space and response space, and can amplify high-frequency formatting artifacts through a self-reinforcing teacher-student loop.
Takeaway: on-policy data alone isn't sufficient for continual learning; dense self-distillation shouldn't be treated as a default stabilizer.
content_html: Continual post-training tries to teach a model new things without erasing what it already knows, and on-policy self-distillation — where a model generates and then scores its own outputs — has looked like a promising way to stabilize that process. This paper revisits the idea and finds the optimism was premature.
extra_html:
When self-distillation helps, and when it doesn't

Studying self-distillation policy optimization (SDPO), the authors find it does accelerate in-domain specialization when teacher signals are stable and well aligned. But it generalizes poorly once the setting shifts out-of-distribution — exactly the situation continual post-training is meant to handle. There, SDPO shows stronger forgetting than plain on-policy RL methods like GRPO, and can collapse outright, while GRPO adapts more conservatively and better preserves prior capabilities.

Why it matters

Digging into why, the authors find denser self-distillation causes larger drift in both parameter space and response space, and can amplify high-frequency formatting artifacts through a self-reinforcing loop — the same model acting as teacher and student feeding its own quirks back to itself. The practical lesson: on-policy data alone isn't sufficient for continual learning, and "add more self-distillation" is not a safe default stabilizer — it can accelerate specialization in the easy case and accelerate collapse in the hard one.

related.title: On the Geometry of On-Policy Distillation
related.hook: On-policy distillation isn't a midpoint between fine-tuning and RL — it carves its own narrow path through parameter space, locking into a low-dimensional subspace early in training.

related.title: Trust Region On-Policy Distillation
related.hook: On-policy distillation breaks when teacher and student disagree too much. TrOPD only trusts the teacher where its supervision is reliable — and skips the rest.

related.title: GRPO: Group Relative Policy Optimization
related.hook: GRPO dropped the value network from PPO and scored each answer against a group of sampled siblings — the cheap RL recipe that made DeepSeek-R1's reasoning trainable.

prereqs.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
prereqs.hook: A big model's softened probabilities say more than hard labels - they reveal how classes relate, so training a small model to mimic them transfers knowledge a one-hot target never could.

flashcards.prompt: What optimistic assumption about on-policy self-distillation does this paper challenge?
flashcards.back_html: That on-policy self-distillation (a model scoring its own generations) reliably mitigates forgetting in continual post-training — the paper shows it can instead cause stronger forgetting or collapse.

flashcards.prompt: In continual post-training, how did SDPO (self-distillation) compare to plain on-policy RL like GRPO?

choices.text: SDPO forgot more and could collapse outright, while GRPO adapted more conservatively and preserved prior capabilities better
SDPO and GRPO performed identically in every setting tested
SDPO always outperformed GRPO regardless of domain shift

flashcards.explanation_html: SDPO helps when teacher signals are stable and in-domain, but under continual post-training with distribution shift it showed stronger forgetting than GRPO, and sometimes collapsed.

flashcards.prompt: Why can denser self-distillation make things worse rather than just 'more thorough'?
flashcards.back_html: Denser self-distillation causes larger drift in parameter and response space, and can amplify high-frequency formatting artifacts through a self-reinforcing loop between the teacher and student roles the same model plays.
